notes:
COUNTS: 38 stations, matching the report's own figure ("thirty-eight lighthouses", line 1237). There are 23 asterisks. Counting Skerryvore, which has no asterisk of its own but shares one with Hynish through the { bracket, makes 24 stations with returns, matching "Twenty-four stations have sent in returns" (line 1238). By the same count, the 14 without returns are: Stornoway, Ushenish, Barra Head, Rona, Kyleakin, Corran Ferry, Lismore Island, Lochindaul, Mull of Kintyre, Sanda, Turnberry, Point of Ayr, Douglas Head and Chickens Rock.

HOW I TRANSCRIBED: Fragments leave out the leading indentation; everything else is kept, including Skerryvore's trailing spaces and ditto mark. The list has no station numbers and no type column (L.H./L.V.), so number and type are null everywhere. I dropped the full stop that ends each character and keeper name, since it only separates the fields ("J. M'Gill." -> "J. M'Gill"); full stops inside abbreviations stay ("alt.", "rev.", "fl.", "Thos."). Coast is the section heading, WEST COAST OF SCOTLAND, for every row; there are no sub-headings. The three Isle of Man lights (Point of Ayr, Douglas Head, Chickens Rock) are listed under this heading too.

HYNISH / SKERRYVORE: The † is printed after "no lights." on the Hynish row, not next to the name. The footnote (lines 1287-1288) says this station was "included by mistake, but retained for convenience, bracketed with the next." So the † belongs to Hynish, and I recorded its marks as "*{ †". Hynish is a signal tower, not a light. I split the row as name "Hynish" and place "Skerryvore Signal Tower, Tyree"; you could also read the name as "Hynish, Skerryvore Signal Tower" with place "Tyree". Skerryvore's marks are just "{", and its return mark comes from the shared asterisk. Its keeper is printed only as a ditto mark ("), which stands for William Crow on the row above. I kept it as '"' in keepers; you'll need to resolve it when building the roll.

UNSURE SPLITS: Several "place" values are really locators rather than counties or islands: "off Tyree", "S.W. of Ross of Mull", "Tobermory", "Loch Eil", "Oban", "Easdale", "Kintyre Sound". Monach Island and Mull of Kintyre have no place printed. Stornoway's and Pladda's characters open with the number of lights ("2 lights, ..." and "2 lights 8 yards apart, ..."); I kept that inside character rather than other. Monach's character "same tower, upp. white fl., low. red, fixed" means two lights in one tower.

SPELLINGS, copied as printed: "Island Glass" (other lists print "Island Ghlais"/Eilean Glas). "Rhu Stoir" (Rhu Stoer / Stoer Head). "Rhuvaal" (Rubh' a' Mhàil). "Dhuheartach" (Dubh Artach). "Skervuile". "Lochindaul" (Loch Indaal). "Devaar" (Davaar). "Chickens Rock" (Chicken Rock). "Point of Ayr" (Point of Ayre, Isle of Man). "Tyree" (Tiree). "Argyleshire". "Rosshire" (Kyleakin is printed as Ross-shire, though the light is usually counted as Skye/Inverness-shire). "M'Gill", "M'Culloch", "M'Lellan" and "M'Donald" use the M' form. "Stornoway" probably means Arnish Point light.

KEEPERS TO CHECK for the roll:
- Charles Black is named at both Devaar and Turnberry. This could be two men with the same name or a printing slip.
- The Ewing name appears three times: J. Ewing (Dhuheartach), John Ewing (Skervuile) and Ralph Ewing (Loch Ryan).
- Laidlaw appears twice: David Laidlaw (Ardnamurchan) and R. Laidlaw (Corsewall).
- Ushenish, Barra Head, Lismore Island, Sanda and Chickens Rock have no keeper named.
